# sevenx_multisite

This section is for administrators, developers and hosts who install Exponential with its default site package, or
who want to understand what that package does before they change or replace it. It answers: what `sevenx_multisite`
is, what it is made of, what its installer script writes, and what you have when the install is finished.

## Contents

1. [In one paragraph](#in-one-paragraph)
2. [The package family](#the-package-family)
3. [What an install gives you](#what-an-install-gives-you)
4. [Where it comes from](#where-it-comes-from)
5. [Pages in this section](#pages-in-this-section)

## In one paragraph

`sevenx_multisite` is a site package (`<type value="site" />` in its `package.xml`) from the vendor `7x`. Its
summary in the package is "MultiSite Default Installation", and the package index of 6.0.15 lists it as "7x MultiSite
Default Installation". It is the package that `exp:install --package` and `exp:kickstarter ini --yes` install when
nothing else is chosen (see [4.3 Site packages](../../../install/04-choosing-an-install-method.md#43-site-packages-what-is-installed)).
It sets up two public websites in one installation, **Fit & Healthy** and **Bold Agency**, plus the administration,
editor and (when the `exp_adminui` extension is present) Admin UI siteaccesses, with page layouts from the
`explayouts` extensions.

## The package family

| Package | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_multisite` | `site` | the site package: settings scripts, the installer, a logo and a thumbnail |
| `sevenx_multisite_clean` | `site` | the same site package without the demo articles, recipes and images |
| `sevenx_classes` | `contentclass` | 33 general content classes (article, folder, image, product ...) |
| `sevenx_multisite_democontent` | `contentobject` | 31 `ng_*` content classes and 291 content objects: the demo content of both sites |
| `sevenx_multisite_democontent_clean` | `contentobject` | the same 31 classes and 35 content objects: the structure, forms and legal pages only |

`sevenx_multisite` requires `sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent`; `sevenx_multisite_clean` requires
`sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent_clean`. Both requirements carry `min-version="5.1"`.

> **Note**
> The layouts of the two sites (21 published layouts with their zones, blocks and rules) are not inside any of these
> packages. The installer seeds them from the `share/*.dba` files of the `sevenx_themes_media` and `explayouts`
> extensions. See [Layouts data and the share .dba files](layouts-data-and-share-dba.md).

## What an install gives you

- The siteaccesses `site` (Fit & Healthy), `bold` and `bold_ger` (Bold Agency in English and German), `admin`,
  `editor`, `adminui` when available, and one extra siteaccess per additional language you chose.
- 60 extensions in `ActiveExtensions` (counted from the installer's `extension_list`), and `expai` and `exp_adminui`
  as access extensions of the administration when they are present.
- Roles for Anonymous, Member, Editor and Partner users, a Restricted section and a Partners user group.
- An RSS feed, settings for the static cache and HTTP cache (installed switched off), search statistics on every
  siteaccess, and settings for links between the two sites.

The full picture is on [What you have after installing](what-you-have-after-installing.md).

## Where it comes from

The source of all five packages is the folder `packages/` of the GitHub repository
[se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage). The installer script descends from
the installer of the `ezwebin_site` package, which the git history shows was added on 2007-03-28; in January 2024 it
moved to `sevenx_site` and on 2026-09-07 it was copied into `sevenx_multisite` as `sevenx-multi-site-installer.php`
(`git log --follow` on that file). The built archives are on the package server under
`exponential/6.0/6.0.15/`, for example
[sevenx_multisite.ezpkg](https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg).

> **Tip**
> To build your own site from this one, read [Making your own site package](../your-own/README.md). 7x and the
> Exponential Foundation encourage you to offer the result to everyone: see
> [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).
